metadata.description: The checks that compare the docs with the code of the libraries (#1044): the generated pages `reference/realm-policies.md` (server-realm-policy), `reference/experimental-features.md` (shared-stability) and `operate/configuration.md` (server-config) must be what their registries render, formatted with Oxfmt and the repo's `.oxfmtrc.json` (`pnpm nx test docs-checks -- -u` rewrites all three); every realm policy field's docs link must name a page of the docs site and a heading on it; the pages flagged `experimental: true` must match the experimental-feature registry one to one (#477); the decision records under docs/adr must name what the registry says they do; and every `path` evidence must exist (#476), which may name any file in the repository, so apps/**/*.ts, libs/**/*.ts and docs/** are inputs. docs-inputs.test.ts reads every project.json and nx.json, and its list of docs files includes CHANGELOG.md. These checks lived in the libraries until #1044. There, their inputs made every docs edit touch the libraries, and the whole-project selection (`affected.legacy`, since turned off) then marked every dependent affected, the auth server and its integration suite among them. Nothing may depend on this project (a module-boundary constraint in .oxlintrc.json), so a docs edit affects it and nothing else. Setting `inputs` replaces the inferred array, so the first six entries are the inferred defaults re-declared, with `oxfmt` added to the external dependencies.
